activation-access-map.rationale: Developer, workspace, and public plugin rollout require existing activation, eligibility, access, revoke, and disable authorities.

activation-onboarding-map.rationale: Account linking, consent, workspace policy, initial connection testing, and support guidance extend the current onboarding lifecycle.

agent-skill-plugin-map.rationale: The feature introduces a reviewed ChatGPT and Codex plugin package, focused MCP tools, metadata snapshots, and optional future skills.

asset-package-map.rationale: Plugin manifests, icons, legal links, screenshots when applicable, and versioned packages use existing asset and package governance.

commercial-usage-map.rationale: Rate limits, quotas, provider costs, public distribution posture, and workspace availability require existing commercial and usage policy.

connector-provider-map.rationale: External actions remain behind connector and provider authority, while MCP receives only bounded results and no credentials or raw provider secrets.

data-model-domain-map.rationale: Client registration, grants, tool catalogs, invocation evidence, confirmations, packages, and review snapshots require reuse-first field classification.

delivery-support-map.rationale: Connection failures, relinking, revocation, unknown outcomes, review findings, and plugin maintenance require existing support and handoff paths.

execution-log-evidence-map.rationale: Initialization, discovery, authorization, denial, invocation, operation, revocation, and review need distinct no-secret lifecycle evidence.

migration-lifecycle-map.rationale: Any justified client, grant, catalog, confirmation, package, or review persistence must use additive governed migration and rollback lifecycles.

observability-release-map.rationale: Endpoint health, metadata parity, OAuth failures, isolation denials, latency, rollout, review, publication, revoke, and rollback require release observability.

platform-resource-graph-map.rationale: OAuth clients, users, tenants, workspaces, Brands, resources, connections, tools, operations, packages, and review snapshots require typed relationships.

platform-runtime-map.rationale: The MCP adapter reuses existing context, authorization, execution, idempotency, readback, reconciliation, evidence, and rollback runtime services.

policy-authority-map.rationale: Scopes, client eligibility, tool visibility, confirmation, external effects, destructive actions, privacy, and tenant rollout require policy authority.

repository-automation-map.rationale: Contract validation, annotation parity, metadata fingerprinting, exact-head evidence, package validation, and no-secret scans require repository automation.

repository-development-map.rationale: Multi-PR delivery, SDK adoption, compatibility changes, generated contracts, CI, review, and release evidence use existing development governance.

session-memory-map.rationale: Follow-up prompts may reuse stable identifiers, but the integration must not require or persist broad conversation transcripts or cross-session secrets.

work-map-coverage-matrix.rationale: The feature must classify every reused or proposed schema object and preserve zero accidental unclassified objects across all current domains.

workflow-task-orchestration-map.rationale: Durable writes, long-running operations, retries, unknown outcomes, status follow-up, compensation, and support escalation reuse workflow orchestration.

Activation & onboarding.rationale: Account linking, consent, rollout, and connection readiness use existing activation and onboarding schema authority.

Agents & intelligence.rationale: Tool selection metadata and optional skills integrate with existing agent, skill, and plugin governance.

Assets & packages.rationale: Plugin packages and presentation assets use existing versioned asset and package lifecycle concepts.

Brand & business.rationale: Brand operating context is exposed only through authorized existing Brand and business projections.

Commercial & usage.rationale: Rate limits, quotas, costs, and distribution policy reuse existing commercial and usage governance.

Connectors & providers.rationale: External provider actions remain behind existing connection ownership, dispatch, and credential boundaries.

Delivery & support.rationale: Relinking, unknown outcomes, review remediation, and support handoff reuse existing support lifecycles.

Developer & API.rationale: A standards-compliant MCP transport and OAuth discovery surface extend the current developer and API domain.

Governance & authority.rationale: Client, scope, tool, confirmation, resource, and rollout decisions remain governed authority records.

Migration & lifecycle.rationale: New persistence is conditional and must follow additive migration, rollback, and closeout authority.

Observability & release.rationale: Metadata parity, endpoint health, invocation evidence, review, publication, and rollback require release evidence.

Platform resources & graph.rationale: Clients, users, tenants, workspaces, Brands, tools, operations, packages, and reviews require typed relationships.

Repository & development.rationale: SDK adoption, contracts, CI, exact-head evidence, and multi-PR delivery use repository governance.

Sessions & memory.rationale: Stable follow-up identifiers are supported while broad conversation collection remains prohibited by design.

Tenancy & identity.rationale: OAuth resource-server and client contracts extend identity while retaining tenant and membership authority.

Workflow & tasks.rationale: Governed mutations, status, retry, reconciliation, compensation, and support remain workflow responsibilities.

implementation_readiness.next_action: Run the canonical Work Map scaffold and complete specification review before any implementation change.
